title: Async — state machine, ValueTask, deadlocks, starvation
exp: `async` builds a state machine; it does not spawn a thread. At 4 YOE you must diagnose deadlocks and thread-pool starvation in production language.
pts: Await I/O; don't block with `.Result` / `.Wait()` on ASP.NET request threads.
**ValueTask<T>** for hot paths that often complete synchronously — await once; don't spray everywhere.
ASP.NET Core has no sync context by default; `ConfigureAwait(false)` still matters in libraries.
**Thread-pool starvation:** sync-over-async or long CPU on pool threads → request queueing.
pr: Find sync-over-async in a sample codebase
Add CancellationToken through a service method

r: Deep dive into Day 3 runtime execution mechanics and threading constraints.
Focus on zero-allocation and lock-free patterns where applicable.
High concurrency contention or unexpected resource exhaustion under load.
Implement resilient backpressure, retries, and circuit breakers.
Balancing low latency, developer ergonomics, and system consistency.
Always state operational cost and complexity trade-offs.

qa.q: Why can .Result deadlock, and how do you fix it?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** If a SynchronizationContext must resume the continuation but the thread is blocked waiting for the task, you deadlock. Fix: async all the way with await; never block in UI/legacy sync contexts. In ASP.NET Core prefer await over Result always.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Async methods compile into an IAsyncStateMachine struct managed by the AsyncMethodBuilder. Awaiting an uncompleted task yields execution back to the caller. Blocking with .Result on a thread bound to a SynchronizationContext causes deadlocks when the continuation waits for the blocked thread.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Sync-over-async (.Result or .Wait()) on ASP.NET request threads rapidly exhausts thread pool threads, leading to HTTP 503 gateway timeouts and request queuing under load.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Async all the way preserves thread pool scalability, but requires passing CancellationToken through all layers and avoiding sync blocking methods everywhere.
